# What is CogPO?

[CogPO](http://www.cogpo.org/), the Cognitive Paradigm Ontology, is a small formal
ontology of behavioral experimental paradigms, built around 2010 to give the
[BrainMap](https://www.brainmap.org/) database a controlled vocabulary for the
experiments it indexes. Its design is described in Turner JA and Laird AR, "The
Cognitive Paradigm Ontology: Design and Application", *Neuroinformatics* 10:57-66
(2012), [DOI 10.1007/s12021-011-9126-x](https://doi.org/10.1007/s12021-011-9126-x). The
work was funded by NIMH grant R01MH084812.

CogPO's distinctive idea is that a paradigm is not a name but a combination of
observable components. Every experimental condition is decomposed along three
dimensions: the **stimulus** presented (its modality, its kind and its role), the
**response** required (the body part and the kind of overt act) and the
**instructions** given to the participant. A paradigm class such as *Stroop Task
Paradigm* is then a named pattern of such conditions. The paradigm layer came from the
BrainMap taxonomy; the dimension vocabularies were new.

This page provides an overview of CogPO and its current state. The page also describes
its influence on and relationship to [HED](https://www.hedtags.org) (Hierarchical Event
Descriptors). [The Catalog vs CogPO](the_catalog_vs_cogpo.md) compares CogPO and the Catalog.
[HED vs CogPO](hed_vs_cogpo.md)

## Two sources

CogPO exists in two forms, and they do not quite agree.

- **The OWL release**, version 1.0 of November 2010, at
  `http://www.cogpo.org/ontologies/CogPOver1.owl`. This is the ontology proper: 199
  classes with definitions, identifiers and provenance annotations, written in RDF/XML
  on the BFO upper ontology with IAO annotation properties. It declares an import of a
  companion file, `CogPOexternalVer1.owl`, but the server returns the main file's bytes
  for that URL too, so there is one file. A second import, the Information Artifact
  Ontology, lives at the OBO Foundry.
- **The wiki** at `www.wiki.cogpo.org`, a MediaWiki with one page per term, opened for
  community comment when the OWL was released. Its curation ran on into 2011 and it
  holds a few terms the OWL never received. Its TLS certificate is invalid, so it is
  reachable over plain http only.

The figures below come from an archive of both taken on 2026-09-22. Nothing in either
source is dated after 2011 and no later release appeared: CogPO is complete as far as it
goes, and unmaintained.

## OWL release summary

| Layer | Classes |
|---|---|
| Behavioral Experimental Paradigm and its subclasses | 84 (83 paradigm classes) |
| Stimulus Modality | 6 top-level, 10 with the four tactile subtypes |
| Explicit Stimulus | 41 |
| Stimulus Role | 0 (the class exists; its four values are on the wiki only) |
| Response Modality | 8 body parts, as unlabeled FMA classes |
| Overt Response | 17 |
| Instructions | 17 |
| Condition, Implicit Stimulus, Covert Response, Response Role | classes with no members |
| Upper-ontology and imported classes | 12 |

Of the 199 classes, 190 carry a label and 181 a definition. The unlabeled nine are the
eight body parts, which are referenced by their Foundational Model of Anatomy
identifiers alone, and `owl:Thing`. 149 classes have an identifier of the form
`COGPO_000nn`; 34 CogPO terms have a name for an IRI instead (`Button Press`,
`Naming_(Overt)_Paradigm`), a sign that the numbering was never finished.

Ten object properties connect the layers: a condition `has_stimulus`,
`has_instructions` and `has_response_type`; a stimulus `has_stimulus_modality`; a
response `has_response_modality`. Every explicit stimulus declares its modality through
a restriction, and six of them (words, letters, digits, syllables, pseudowords, Braille
dots) declare two. Three named individuals illustrate the design with one FBIRN
auditory oddball task and its two conditions.

## The paradigm layer

The 83 paradigm classes are direct children of *Behavioral Experimental Paradigm*, except
that *Oddball Discrimination* has *Auditory Oddball* and *Visual Oddball* beneath it. The
wiki adds three more (Delayed Match To Sample, Sleep, Tower of London) and lacks the two
Oddball subclasses, so it lists 84.

Almost every definition has the same form: "A Behavioral Experimental Paradigm in which,
in at least one of the conditions, subjects ...". The "at least one of the conditions"
clause is deliberate: CogPO was built to code published experiments, which routinely
combine paradigms, and a class is meant to be assigned whenever any condition fits. The
definitions also say which classes to co-code (a passive face-viewing study is coded as
Face Monitor or Discrimination but not also as Passive Viewing).

The list reflects its origin. Alongside Stroop, Flanker, Go/No-Go, n-back, Sternberg,
Simon, Posner, Task Switching, Wisconsin Card Sorting and Mental Rotation stand
Acupuncture, Breath-Holding, Chewing or Swallowing, Eating or Drinking, Micturition,
Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation, Flashing Checkerboard, Whistling and Video Games:
anything BrainMap needed to describe an imaging experiment, whether or not it is a task
in any cognitive sense.

## The dimensions

The dimension vocabularies are CogPO's lasting contribution, and they are small enough to
list. *Stimulus Modality* has six values (visual, auditory, tactile, olfactory,
gustatory, interoceptive), with electrical, pain, pressure and thermal as subtypes of
tactile. *Explicit Stimulus* has 41 values from words, faces and tones to random dots,
fixation point, food, odor, heat, infusion and TMS. *Overt Response* has 17, from button
press, saccade and speech to blink, grasp, swallow and micturate. *Instructions* has 17
verbs: attend, count, detect, discriminate, encode, fixate, generate, imagine, move,
name, read, recall, repeat, rest, sing, smile, track. *Response Modality* is eight body
parts (hand, foot, mouth, face, arm, leg, shoulder, pelvis). *Stimulus Role* has four
values on the wiki (target, non-target, feedback, reward) and none in the OWL.

Every value has a definition, most of them dictionary definitions with the source
cited, and 75 classes cite a BrainMap paper as the use that motivated the term. The
[dimension mapping](dimension_mapping.md) page lists all of them.

## Curation state

The OWL annotations record where the work stopped.

| Curation status (OWL) | Classes |
|---|---|
| `pending_final_vetting` | 142 |
| none recorded | 38 |
| `definition_incomplete` | 17 |
| `curation_complete` | 2 |

Every dated class is dated 2010. The wiki's later pass marked most terms complete: of
184 term pages, 92 say "curation complete Aug 2011", 77 "curation complete Dec 2010",
5 "curation complete Sept 2011" and 9 remain "pending final vetting". 25 wiki
definitions differ from their OWL text, mostly small rewordings; one, the Stroop
definition, has acquired a spam link.

Neither source carries a license statement.

## What CogPO does not have

CogPO has no layer for cognitive processes: nothing says what a paradigm measures or
which mental function it engages. It has no named variations, no inclusion tests and no
references per paradigm beyond the occasional BrainMap citation on a definition. And the
decomposition into conditions, which is its central design, is populated for exactly
one example task. The dimension vocabularies exist; the paradigm-to-dimension
assignments that would use them were never published.
